{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-03",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Payment event producer", "Kafka payments topic", "Internal consumer services"],
    "dataStores": ["Kafka payments topic (event log)"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Payment service to Kafka broker", "Kafka broker to any internal consumer"],
    "dataClasses": ["payment", "pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Every internal service can read cardholder and customer data from the payments topic",
      "scenario": "The topic is readable by all internal services, so any service account, or an attacker who compromises the least protected internal service or developer laptop with broker credentials, can subscribe and harvest card BIN, last four digits, amount and customer id for every payment. That is a payment-data breach across the whole customer base and pulls every consuming service into PCI DSS scope. No consumer-level authorization is described.",
      "component": "Kafka payments topic",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Payment events are published to a Kafka topic that every internal service can consume." },
        { "quote": "Events include the card BIN, last four digits, amount and customer id." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.1.1", "V8.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-200", "CWE-284"],
      "plainLanguage": "Any internal system can read card details and customer ids for every payment, so one hacked service leaks everyone's payment data.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict payments topic reads to an allow-list of consumers",
        "given": "a payments Kafka topic carrying card BIN, last four and customer id",
        "when": "a service or user attempts to subscribe or read from the topic",
        "then": "the broker authorizes the request against a per-consumer ACL allow-list and denies every principal not explicitly approved for payment data"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Card fields published when consumers do not need them",
      "scenario": "The event payload carries card BIN plus last four digits and customer id together for all consumers, regardless of need. BIN plus last four plus amount plus customer id is enough for convincing payment-related social engineering and card-issuer fingerprinting, and the data persists for the whole topic retention period, so a single later read exposes historical payments, not just live traffic.",
      "component": "Payment event payload",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Events include the card BIN, last four digits, amount and customer id." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V14.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-359"],
      "plainLanguage": "The event carries more card detail than most services need, and it stays in the log for as long as the topic keeps messages.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Minimise and tokenise card data in payment events",
        "given": "a payment event schema",
        "when": "an event is published to the payments topic",
        "then": "it contains only a payment token or surrogate reference instead of card BIN and last four digits, unless a named consumer has an approved business need delivered on a separate restricted topic"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Any internal producer can forge payment events",
      "scenario": "Because the topic is a shared internal bus with no producer authentication or authorization described, any internal service or attacker with broker access can publish fake payment events with chosen amounts and customer ids. Downstream consumers such as ledgers, fulfilment or analytics would treat them as real payments, enabling fraudulent order release or corrupted financial reporting.",
      "component": "Kafka payments topic (producer side)",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Payment events are published to a Kafka topic that every internal service can consume." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306", "CWE-345"],
      "plainLanguage": "Nothing stops another internal system from writing fake payment messages that the rest of the business trusts as real.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Authenticate and restrict producers to the payments topic",
        "given": "the payments topic",
        "when": "a client attempts to publish a payment event",
        "then": "the broker requires mutual-TLS or SASL authentication and allows writes only from the payment service principal, rejecting all other producers"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Consumers cannot tell a replayed or altered payment event from a genuine one",
      "scenario": "Events carry amount and customer id with no described signature, idempotency key or event provenance. An attacker with topic write access, or a buggy or malicious replay of the log, can re-emit or alter payment events; consumers that credit balances or trigger fulfilment on each event would double-process payments. The shared internal bus means any consumer can also act as a producer.",
      "component": "Payment event schema and consumers",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Events include the card BIN, last four digits, amount and customer id." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V11.3.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-345"],
      "plainLanguage": "A payment message could be copied or edited and replayed, and services would process the same payment twice.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Integrity-protect and de-duplicate payment events",
        "given": "a payment event on the payments topic",
        "when": "a consumer processes the event",
        "then": "it verifies a producer signature over the payload and ignores any event whose unique event id has already been processed"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No record of which service read payment data",
      "scenario": "With open consumption by every internal service and no described consumer identity, there is no reliable way to prove after an incident which service or person pulled card data from the topic. During a payment-data breach investigation this prevents scoping the exposure and lets an insider deny having read the data.",
      "component": "Kafka broker access records",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Payment events are published to a Kafka topic that every internal service can consume." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "If card data leaks we cannot tell which system or person read it, because consumers are not identified.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Record authenticated consumer identity for payment data reads",
        "given": "an authenticated consumer of the payments topic",
        "when": "it joins a consumer group or fetches records",
        "then": "the broker records the consumer principal, group and topic in tamper-evident access records retained for the payment-data investigation window"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "A low-trust service gains payment-level access just by joining the internal bus",
      "scenario": "Granting access to the whole internal estate means a low-trust component (for example an internal reporting or test tool, or a newly onboarded team's service) inherits payment-data privileges without any approval step. An attacker who only needs to compromise the weakest internal service effectively obtains payment-system-level read access, bypassing the controls placed around the payment service itself.",
      "component": "Internal consumer services",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Payment events are published to a Kafka topic that every internal service can consume." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-862", "CWE-266"],
      "plainLanguage": "Being on the internal network is treated as permission to see payment data, so breaking into any small service is as good as breaking into payments.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Require explicit approval before a service receives payment-topic access",
        "given": "a service requesting access to payment events",
        "when": "access is granted",
        "then": "it is granted per-service by a named payment-data owner with a recorded business justification and review date, and default internal access confers no payment-topic rights"
      }
    }
  ]
}

This gives bulk cardholder data for many customers with no additional privilege, and widens PCI DSS scope to every consuming service.",
      "component": "Kafka payment events topic",
      "likelihood": 4,

        "given": "payment events containing card BIN, last four and customer id are published to Kafka",
        "when": "a service attempts to subscribe to the payments topic",
        "then": "the broker denies the subscription unless that service principal is on an explicit per-topic read allow-list, reviewed and approved by the payments owner"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Card BIN plus last four and customer id are broadcast when consumers do not need them",
      "scenario": "Consumers that only need an amount and an order reference receive card BIN, last four digits and customer id. BIN plus last four identifies the issuer and the specific card and, joined with customer id, lets an insider or an attacker in any consumer build a cardholder profile usable for convincing payment-fraud phone scams. Copies then spread into every consumer's logs and datastores.",
      "component": "Payment event payload",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Events include the card BIN, last four digits, amount and customer id." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],

      "plainLanguage": "The events carry more card data than most consumers need, so sensitive data spreads everywhere.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Minimise cardholder data in published events",
        "given": "a payment event is constructed for publication",
        "when": "the event is serialised to the Kafka topic",
        "then": "it contains no card BIN, and card identification is limited to a non-reversible payment token, with last four digits published only on a separate restricted topic for consumers with a documented need"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Any internal service can publish forged payment events",
      "scenario": "The design names no producer authorisation or event authenticity check. An attacker who gains any internal service credential, or a buggy service, publishes fabricated payment events (for example a large amount for another customer id) onto the topic. Downstream consumers such as ledger, analytics, loyalty or fulfilment treat them as genuine payments, causing incorrect balances, released goods or fraudulent credits.",
      "component": "Kafka payment events topic (produce path)",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Payment events are published to a Kafka topic that every internal service can consume." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-345", "CWE-862"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could inject fake payment messages and downstream systems would believe them.",

        "given": "the payments topic accepts events",
        "when": "a client attempts to write to the topic",
        "then": "the broker rejects the write unless the authenticated principal is the payment service, and consumers reject any event whose integrity signature or schema-registry provenance does not validate"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "No access control model stated between the payment service and the broker",
      "scenario": "Because consumption is granted to 'every internal service', the topic effectively has no authorisation decision at all: possession of network reachability or a shared broker credential is enough. An attacker who lands on any internal host escalates from no payment access to full read, and potentially write, of the payment stream without touching the payment service itself.",
      "component": "Kafka broker authentication and ACLs",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Payment events are published to a Kafka topic that every internal service can consume." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306", "CWE-284"],
      "plainLanguage": "Being on the internal network is treated as permission to read payments; it should not be.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Per-principal broker authentication for payment topics",
        "given": "the Kafka cluster hosting payment events",
        "when": "any client connects",
        "then": "it must authenticate with a unique, per-service identity (mTLS or SASL) and all payment-topic operations are denied by default unless an ACL grants them"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Payment data persists in topic retention and consumer replays long after it is needed",
      "scenario": "Kafka retains the log, so card BIN, last four and customer id for historical payments stay readable on the brokers and can be replayed from the earliest offset by any permitted consumer. An attacker who obtains consumer access at any point in the future, or who gets a broker disk or backup, retrieves the whole payment history rather than only live traffic.",
      "component": "Kafka topic log (payment events)",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Payment events are published to a Kafka topic that every internal service can consume. Events include the card BIN, last four digits, amount and customer id." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-212", "CWE-311"],
      "plainLanguage": "Old payment events stay stored and can be replayed, so one break-in exposes months of card data.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bound retention and encrypt payment event storage",
        "given": "payment events written to the Kafka log",
        "when": "the configured retention period elapses",
        "then": "the records are deleted (or the field-level encryption keys for them are destroyed), retention is set to the shortest documented business need, and payment-topic segments are encrypted at rest"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Payment events carry no verifiable producer identity, so a disputed event cannot be attributed",
      "scenario": "The design describes events only by their payload fields. With no signed producer identity or event id in the schema, a fraudulent or duplicated payment event discovered later cannot be traced to the service or credential that published it, and the real payment service cannot prove it did not emit it. This blocks fraud investigation and dispute resolution for payment records.",
      "component": "Payment event schema",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Events include the card BIN, last four digits, amount and customer id." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778", "CWE-346"],
      "plainLanguage": "If a bad payment event shows up, nobody can prove which system actually sent it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Attributable payment events",
        "given": "a payment event published to the topic",
        "when": "an investigator examines it",
        "then": "the event contains a unique event id, producing service identity and timestamp bound by the broker's authenticated principal, and the broker records the authenticated producer for each write"
      }
    }
  ]
}
